prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1190; do not mention it.)
text:
I am writing to advise that this office now represents the injured party in connection with the collision described in your file. The client was injured in a low-speed head-on collision and is actively receiving medical care for those injuries. Effective immediately, please direct all communications regarding this claim to our office and do not contact the client directly, either by telephone, in writing, or in person. If the client's representatives or agents contact you, please refer them to us.

We also request that you disclose the bodily injury and property damage limits of every policy that may apply to this loss, including any excess or umbrella coverage, and confirm the identity of the policyholder and all listed drivers. Please provide this information in writing within thirty days.

Finally, we ask that your company preserve all evidence relating to this collision. This includes photographs, vehicle inspection reports, repair estimates, telematics or event data recorder downloads, recorded statements, adjuster notes, and any other materials in your possession. Please suspend any routine deletion or disposal of these records until the matter is resolved.
